Privacy notice

This notice explains how personal information is collected and used when you visit this website, contact me, enquire about work, subscribe to updates or otherwise engage with my professional services.

Last updated: 13 October 2026

In brief

I use personal information to respond to relevant enquiries, arrange and deliver agreed work, maintain necessary professional and financial records, send updates where you have opted in, and keep this website secure. I do not sell personal information.

Overview

This privacy notice explains how I handle personal information in connection with https://rjmlaird.co.uk and related professional activity.

It is intended to help you understand what information may be collected, why it is needed, how it is used, who may receive it, how long it may be retained and the choices and rights available to you.

This notice does not replace the privacy notices of independent websites, platforms or organisations that you may visit through links from this site. Those organisations are responsible for their own information and data-handling practices.

Who is responsible

Ryan J. M. Laird is the data controller for personal information collected through this website.

In this notice, “I”, “me” and “my” mean Ryan J. M. Laird. “You” means a visitor to this site, an enquirer, client, collaborator, event organiser, editor, journalist, recruiter, student, parent, guardian or other person whose information is provided in connection with my work.

What this covers

This notice applies when you:

  • Visit or interact with rjmlaird.co.uk
  • Use a contact form or email address published on this site
  • Ask about advisory, communication, digital, editorial or collaboration work
  • Request a talk, panel contribution, interview or media comment
  • Subscribe to a newsletter or other optional updates, where available
  • Follow a link to the separate booking portal at booking.rjmlaird.co.uk
  • Are referred to Impact Orbit Collective for organisation-level work

The booking portal, payment providers, calendar providers and other independent services may provide additional privacy information when you use them. Please read those notices alongside this one where applicable.

Information collected

The information collected depends on how you use the site and the context of your interaction. It may include the following categories.

Contact and identity information

  • Name
  • Email address
  • Telephone number, where you provide it
  • Organisation, role, sector and professional profile information
  • Preferred contact method and communication preferences

Enquiry and project information

  • Your message and the reason you are contacting me
  • Project, service, event or collaboration context
  • Relevant links, documents or attachments you choose to share
  • Timescales, budget information and intended outcomes, where provided
  • Meeting notes, correspondence and agreed next steps

Speaking, media and public-engagement information

  • Event, programme, publication or project name
  • Audience, subject, brief, format and session requirements
  • Date, location, online platform, travel and accessibility information
  • Recording, photography, editorial, licensing or usage requirements

Technical and usage information

  • IP address and approximate location derived from it
  • Browser, device, operating system and screen information
  • Pages viewed, referring source, site interactions and error information
  • Security, performance and service-operation logs
  • Cookie identifiers and consent preferences, where applicable

Financial and transaction information

If work is agreed, relevant records may include invoices, payment status, tax information and associated correspondence. Payment-card details are handled by the relevant payment provider and are not stored directly by me unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Information you choose to provide

You may choose to provide additional information through forms, email, documents, calls or other communications. Please provide only what is relevant to your enquiry or the work being discussed.

Where information comes from

Most personal information is collected directly from you, for example when you:

  • Submit a form, send an email or arrange a call
  • Subscribe to optional updates
  • Provide information during a project, event or collaboration
  • Use the website and its essential or consented technologies

In limited circumstances, information may also come from:

  • A colleague, employer, client, parent, guardian or event organiser acting on your behalf
  • Publicly available professional sources, such as your organisation’s website or public professional profile
  • A referral partner, collaborator or associated organisation, where relevant to a legitimate enquiry
  • Service providers that support website, booking, payment or communication processes

If I receive your information from someone else in a way that requires further privacy information to be provided, I will do so as required by applicable law.

Where I rely on legitimate interests, I consider whether the processing is necessary, proportionate and reasonably expected in the context of the relationship or interaction. I do not use legitimate interests where your rights and interests override those interests.

Sensitive information

Please do not send special-category personal information through this website unless it is necessary for a specific agreed purpose. This may include information about health, disability, racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, political opinions, trade-union membership, genetics, biometrics, sex life or sexual orientation.

If sensitive information is genuinely needed, for example to understand an accessibility requirement or meet a safeguarding responsibility, I will explain the purpose, the relevant legal condition and any additional handling arrangements before or when the information is collected.

Sharing information

Personal information is not sold. It is shared only where necessary to operate this website, respond to a request, provide agreed work, meet a legal obligation, protect rights and safety, or with your agreement.

Service providers

Relevant service providers may process information on my behalf. These may include providers of hosting, content delivery, security, forms, email, calendars, document storage, newsletter delivery, analytics, booking, invoicing and payment services.

Professional advisers and authorities

Impact Orbit Collective referrals

Some organisation-level work is more appropriately delivered throughImpact Orbit Collective. This includes, for example, wider communication strategies, multi-part digital projects, retained support, campaigns, larger training programmes or team-based delivery.

Where your enquiry is suitable for referral, relevant information may be shared with Impact Orbit Collective only to the extent needed to discuss or progress the request, and where appropriate with your knowledge or agreement.

Business changes

If a business, service or relevant assets are reorganised, transferred or acquired, personal information may be shared with relevant professional advisers and prospective parties where lawful and subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

International transfers

Depending on the provider and destination, this may include UK adequacy regulations, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement, the UK Addendum to EU Standard Contractual Clauses, or another lawful transfer mechanism.

When information is no longer needed, it will be securely deleted, anonymised or archived only where continued retention is necessary.

Security

Reasonable technical and organisational measures are used to protect personal information against unauthorised access, accidental loss, misuse, alteration, disclosure or destruction.

These measures may include:

  • Access controls and least-privilege access to relevant systems
  • Strong account security and multi-factor authentication where available
  • Encrypted connections where supported by the service provider
  • Reputable hosting, payment, booking and communication providers
  • Regular review of systems, suppliers and access arrangements
  • Appropriate procedures for responding to suspected data incidents

No online system can be guaranteed completely secure. Please avoid sending unnecessary sensitive information through ordinary email or website forms.

Cookies and analytics

This website may use cookies, local storage and similar technologies. Some are necessary for security, accessibility, form handling and core website functionality. Others may support analytics, embedded content or service improvement.

Non-essential cookies and similar technologies should be used only with the consent required by applicable law. You can find more detail in the cookie notice.

Your rights

Depending on the circumstances and the legal basis used, you may have the right to:

  • Ask for access to the personal information held about you
  • Ask for inaccurate or incomplete information to be corrected
  • Ask for information to be erased in certain circumstances
  • Ask for processing to be restricted in certain circumstances
  • Object to processing based on legitimate interests
  • Receive a portable copy of certain information you provided
  • Withdraw consent at any time where consent is relied upon
  • Complain to the UK Information Commissioner’s Office

How to make a request

To exercise a right, emailprivacy@rjmlaird.co.uk. Please state what you are requesting and provide enough information to help identify the relevant records.

I may need to verify your identity before completing a request. Requests are normally handled without charge, although a reasonable fee or refusal may be permitted where a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive.

Children and young people

This main website is primarily intended for professional, educational and organisational audiences. If services for a person under 18 are offered, enquiries and arrangements should normally be made by a parent, guardian or school.

Where information about a child or young person is processed, it will be handled only as necessary for the relevant activity and in line with applicable safeguarding arrangements.

See the safeguarding policy for further information once published.

Changes to this notice

This notice may be updated where services, suppliers, website technology, legal requirements or data-handling arrangements change. The current version will always be published on this page with the date it was last updated.

Where a significant change materially affects how information is used, I will take appropriate steps to bring it to the attention of affected people where reasonably practicable.
